name: Netherlands
summary_text: The Netherlands is a very safe destination for transgender visitors. Official guidance prepared for WorldPride Amsterdam 2026 confirms there are no visa or entry restrictions based on gender identity, passports with amended or "X" gender markers are accepted, and no medical documentation is needed. Discrimination based on gender identity is prohibited by law, and a 2025 law makes discriminatory motive an aggravating factor that can increase penalties by a third. The country's institutions are strongly supportive: Amsterdam operates dedicated LGBTQIA+ reporting networks, and the mayor and police committed to priority investigation of Pride-period incidents in 2026. The capital is among Europe's safer cities for ordinary crime. One caution: reported discrimination and violence against LGBTQ people has risen sharply since 2022 (anti-trans reports rose about 50% in the last year), and surveys indicate many queer residents avoid public displays of affection. For a visitor this translates mainly to a risk of harassment or verbal abuse, particularly late at night, rather than systematic danger.

sources.title: Safety and travel information - Pride Amsterdam 2027
sources.claim_summary: WorldPride Amsterdam 2026 safety and travel page: border/airport procedures, Schengen passport rules, Schiphol logistics, city caution, and a dedicated section for transgender and non-binary visitors; notes the Netherlands ranks #13 on the ILGA Rainbow Map 2026.

sources.title: Netherlands | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): progressive laws with gaps - legal gender change still requires a medical expert letter; 'X' marker only via a 3-9 month court procedure; the Transgender Act (self-ID) was withdrawn in July 2025; compensation offered to those sterilised under previous rules.

sources.title: Combating discrimination and violence against LGBTIQ+ people in the Netherlands | Government.nl
sources.claim_summary: Dutch government page on combating discrimination and violence against LGBTIQ+ people: in 2022 one third of police discrimination reports concerned sexual orientation; over 10% of LGBTIQ+ people have experienced physical or sexual violence (17% of trans people, 22% of intersex people); incidents of verbal abuse, intimidation and violence increased sharply per the 2023 National Programme against Discrimination and Racism; lists government measures.

sources.title: New Justice and Security laws as of 1 July 2025 | Government.nl
sources.claim_summary: Government.nl overview of new justice and security laws from 1 July 2025 - includes expansion of victims' rights and protection of victim data in criminal case records (general context, not trans-specific).

Equaldex data for the Netherlands: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change legal but requires medical diagnosis, nonbinary recognised, hate-crime protections cover sexual orientation only, discrimination illegal, employment/housing discrimination prohibited on SOGI, conversion therapy banned, bathroom access protected. High public support (52% support LGBT openness; ranked #2 of 121 regions as a 'good place').

sources.title: Reports of discrimination targeting LGBTQ jumped 81 pct. in the Netherlands since 2022 | NL Times
sources.claim_summary: NL Times (April 2026): reports of discrimination targeting LGBTQ people jumped 81% since 2022 (4,800 reports last year, +7.5% vs 2024); reports about trans people specifically rose 51% in a year (264 to 399); COC called it 'extremely worrying', noting only six convictions for anti-LGBTQIA+ discrimination last year.

sources.title: Video: More than 70 report discrimination at the start of WorldPride in Amsterdam | NL Times
sources.claim_summary: NL Times (July 2026): more than 70 people reported discrimination during the start of WorldPride in Amsterdam (via the RITA platform) - most from festival-goers leaving the Milkshake festival and Pride Walk participants; RITA fears the reports are 'only a fraction of the total'; safer spaces set up in hotels, museums and public buildings.

sources.title: Amsterdam broadens reporting points for anti-LGBTQIA+ violence during world pride | NL Times
sources.claim_summary: NL Times (June 2026): Amsterdam broadened reporting points for anti-LGBTQIA+ violence during World Pride - 'Safer Spaces' across the city (Nieuwe Kerk, Stedelijk Museum, Stadsarchief, hotels) plus a central RITA location; incidents to be investigated with priority; 1.4 million visitors expected.

sources.title: Amsterdam to tackle discrimination, violent incidents with priority during World Pride | NL Times
sources.claim_summary: NL Times (June 2026): Amsterdam will tackle discrimination and violent incidents with priority during World Pride - Mayor Halsema's letter to the council; police/enforcer/organiser agreements to act quickly; recent Prides saw 25-45 anti-LGBTQIA+ incident reports.

sources.title: National frameworks to address hate crime in the Netherlands | HCRW
sources.claim_summary: OSCE/ODIHR page on the Netherlands' national hate-crime frameworks: Dutch legislation does not include a definition of hate crime; police record hate crimes, hate speech and other discrimination incidents.

Dutch Government 'LGBT and Gender Equality Policy Plan of the Netherlands 2011-2015' (Council of Europe repository): the cabinet's policy - combating discrimination and penalising it more severely, increasing safety so same-sex couples can walk hand-in-hand and young people can come out safely, and furthering women's labour-market participation.
